payload.title: String Calculator First Release Specification
payload.summary: A bounded Python String Calculator with one public add operation and one installed command, sharing a single calculation path and supported by public-contract verification and human-reviewable TDD evidence.
payload.problem_statement: Software developers need a small, predictable String Calculator whose supported Number List behavior is explicit and verifiable. Delivery practitioners also need evidence that reviewed intent moved through incremental TDD, repeatable verification, and human-owned review without importing later kata stages or unrelated product scope.

items.title: Usable bounded calculator
items.statement: Deliver a usable String Calculator through a public Python operation and an installed command-line interface for the agreed integer-list use cases.
items.rationale: The release must provide an actual consumable result while remaining bounded to reviewed behavior.

source_notes.text: The problem statement and solution require a usable, bounded String Calculator exposed through Python and an installed command.

items.title: Traceable delivery journey
items.statement: Provide human-reviewable evidence that the product progressed from reviewed intent through incremental TDD and repeatable verification.
items.rationale: A finished solution alone does not demonstrate the requested delivery journey.

source_notes.text: The source requires traceable delivery evidence, visible red-green progression, comparable verification, and human-owned review.

items.title: Empty Number List returns zero
items.statement: The calculator MUST return integer zero when the supplied Number List is empty.
items.rationale: The absence of values needs an explicit and predictable result.
acceptance: Calling the public add operation with an empty string returns 0.
The result is an integer.
The empty case does not produce a Negative-number Rejection.

source_notes.text: User story 3 and the implementation decisions define an empty Number List as zero.
The controlled language says an empty Number List represents zero.

items.title: Single non-negative token
items.statement: The calculator MUST return the numeric value of one non-negative Integer Token.
items.rationale: The simplest non-empty valid Number List must work directly.
acceptance: Calling add with 1 returns integer 1.
Calling add with 42 returns integer 42.
No delimiter is required when the Number List contains one token.

source_notes.text: User story 4 requires one non-negative Integer Token to return its value.

items.title: Comma-delimited summation
items.statement: The calculator MUST sum Integer Tokens separated by exactly one comma delimiter.
items.rationale: Comma-separated values are the conventional Number List form in this release.
acceptance: Calling add with 1,2 returns 3.
Calling add with 10,20,30 returns 60.
Every valid comma-delimited token contributes once to the sum.

source_notes.text: User story 5 and the Number List decision require comma-separated Integer Tokens to be summed.

items.title: Line-feed-delimited summation
items.statement: The calculator MUST sum Integer Tokens separated by actual line-feed delimiters.
items.rationale: A Number List may span lines without changing calculation semantics.
acceptance: Calling add with two tokens separated by an actual line-feed returns their sum.
A Number List spanning multiple lines is accepted when every token is valid.
The line-feed is interpreted as a delimiter rather than token content.

source_notes.text: User story 6 requires actual line feeds to delimit Integer Tokens.
Delimiter is defined as a comma or line-feed character between adjacent Integer Tokens.

items.title: Mixed supported delimiters
items.statement: The calculator MUST accept commas and actual line feeds together in one Number List and sum all tokens consistently.
items.rationale: Both supported delimiter forms may coexist in one valid input.
acceptance: Calling add with 1 followed by a line-feed and then 2,3 returns 6.
Comma and line-feed occurrences may appear in either order.
Mixing supported delimiters does not change token numeric meaning.

source_notes.text: User story 7 and the Number List decision explicitly permit commas and line feeds in the same list.

items.title: No arbitrary token-count limit
items.statement: The calculator MUST accept any number of valid Integer Tokens without an arbitrary product-level maximum count.
items.rationale: Valid lists must not be restricted to introductory examples.
acceptance: A valid Number List containing more tokens than the basic examples is summed successfully.
The implementation exposes no documented product-level token-count maximum.
All tokens in a valid long list contribute to the returned sum.

source_notes.text: User story 8 and the implementation decisions prohibit an arbitrary product-level token-count limit.

items.title: Leading zeros retain numeric meaning
items.statement: The calculator MUST interpret ASCII decimal tokens with leading zeros by their integer value.
items.rationale: Decimal spelling must not alter the value included in the sum.
acceptance: Calling add with 0007 returns 7.
Calling add with 01,002 returns 3.
Leading zeros do not cause octal or textual interpretation.

source_notes.text: User story 9 and the implementation decisions require leading zeros to retain numeric meaning.
Integer Token says leading zeros do not change the token value.

items.title: Negative zero is not rejected
items.statement: The calculator MUST interpret negative-zero spellings as zero and MUST NOT reject them as negative values.
items.rationale: Negative-number rejection is based on numeric value rather than the presence of a minus sign.
acceptance: Calling add with -0 returns 0.
Calling add with -000,2 returns 2.
A negative-zero occurrence is absent from any rejection diagnostic.

source_notes.text: User story 10 and the implementation decisions explicitly treat negative zero as zero.
Integer Token defines negative zero as zero.

items.title: Reject the entire list for negative values
items.statement: The calculator MUST reject the entire Number List when any parsed value is below zero and MUST NOT return a partial sum.
items.rationale: A partial result could be mistaken for a successful calculation.
acceptance: Calling add with 1,-2,3 raises ValueError.
No integer sum is returned when one or more values are negative.
Non-negative tokens do not suppress rejection caused by another token.

source_notes.text: User story 11 requires any negative value to reject the full list without a partial sum.
Negative-number Rejection is defined as an alternative to a partial sum.

items.title: Report every negative occurrence
items.statement: A Negative-number Rejection MUST identify every negative occurrence in encounter order.
items.rationale: Users need to map each rejected occurrence back to the supplied Number List.
acceptance: Input -1,2,-3 reports both -1 and -3.
The diagnostic orders -1 before -3 because that is their encounter order.
No negative occurrence is omitted when positives appear between negatives.

source_notes.text: User story 12 requires every negative occurrence to be reported in encounter order.
Negative-number Rejection reports every negative value in encounter order.

items.title: Preserve repeated negatives
items.statement: A Negative-number Rejection MUST retain duplicate negative occurrences.
items.rationale: Deduplication would hide invalid occurrences in the input.
acceptance: Input -2,-2 reports -2 twice.
Duplicate negative values remain in their original relative positions.
The diagnostic does not convert negative occurrences into a set.

source_notes.text: User story 13 requires repeated negative values to remain visible in the rejection.
Negative-number Rejection explicitly includes duplicates.

items.title: Canonical negative diagnostics
items.statement: A Negative-number Rejection MUST render each below-zero value as canonical decimal text without leading zeros.
items.rationale: Equivalent negative spellings need consistent diagnostics.
acceptance: Input -001 reports -1.
Input -01,-0002 reports -1, -2 in that order.
Canonical rendering changes spelling only and preserves occurrence count.

source_notes.text: User story 14 and the rejection-format decision require canonical negative values without leading zeros.
The glossary requires canonical decimal negative values without leading zeros.

items.title: Public Python add operation
items.statement: The string_calculator package MUST export add(numbers: str) -> int directly from its public interface.
items.rationale: Python consumers must not depend on internal module organization.
acceptance: from string_calculator import add succeeds in an installed environment.
The public operation accepts one string argument named numbers.
Successful calls return an integer.

source_notes.text: User stories 1 and 2 and the implementation decisions define the direct public add signature.

items.title: Python rejection error type and text
items.statement: The public add operation MUST raise ValueError with text beginning negative numbers not allowed: followed by canonical negative occurrences separated by comma and space.
items.rationale: Python callers need a stable rejection seam and complete diagnostic.
acceptance: Input -1 raises ValueError with text negative numbers not allowed: -1.
Input -1,-2 raises text ending -1, -2.
The operation raises rather than returning the diagnostic as a successful value.

source_notes.text: The implementation decisions prescribe ValueError and the exact negative numbers not allowed diagnostic format.

items.title: Installed command with positional input
items.statement: The project MUST install a string-calculator command that accepts one Number List as a positional argument for supported invocations.
items.rationale: The calculator must be directly scriptable from a shell.
acceptance: The string-calculator executable is available after project installation.
A supported invocation supplies exactly one Number List positional argument.
The command routes the supplied argument to calculator behavior.

source_notes.text: User story 15 and the implementation decisions require an installed string-calculator command with one positional Number List.

items.title: CLI actual line-feed support
items.statement: The installed command MUST accept actual shell-quoted line feeds as Number List delimiters.
items.rationale: Command-line calculation behavior must match the Python operation for supported delimiters.
acceptance: A shell argument containing an actual line-feed between 1 and 2 produces 3.
The command passes the actual line-feed through as delimiter content.
The two-character backslash-n sequence is not used as evidence for this requirement.

source_notes.text: User story 16 requires shell-quoted actual line feeds to work as delimiters.

items.title: CLI successful output contract
items.statement: On successful calculation the installed command MUST write only the decimal sum and one trailing newline to standard output, write nothing to standard error, and exit zero.
items.rationale: Other programs need reliable machine-consumable success behavior.
acceptance: A successful invocation for 1,2 writes exactly 3 followed by one newline to stdout.
The same successful invocation writes zero bytes to stderr.
The process exit status is 0.

source_notes.text: User story 17 and the CLI decisions prescribe stdout, stderr, newline, and exit-zero behavior.

items.title: CLI negative rejection contract
items.statement: On Negative-number Rejection the installed command MUST write the Python error text and one trailing newline to standard error, write no sum to standard output, and exit nonzero.
items.rationale: Automation must not mistake rejected input for a successful sum.
acceptance: An invocation containing -1 writes negative numbers not allowed: -1 followed by one newline to stderr.
The rejected invocation writes zero bytes to stdout.
The rejected invocation exits with a nonzero status.

source_notes.text: User story 18 and the CLI decisions prescribe stderr, no stdout sum, and nonzero status for negative input.

items.title: Number List grammar
items.statement: A supported Number List MUST be either empty or one or more Integer Tokens separated by exactly one comma or actual line-feed delimiter.
items.rationale: The public input language needs an explicit supported grammar.
acceptance: The empty string is classified as a Number List.
A non-empty supported list alternates Integer Tokens and single supported delimiters.
Both delimiter forms may occur in one Number List.

source_notes.text: The implementation decisions define Number List syntax and supported delimiter forms.
The repository context defines Number List as zero or more Integer Tokens separated by Delimiters.

items.title: Integer Token grammar
items.statement: An Integer Token MUST contain ASCII decimal digits with an optional leading minus sign and MUST NOT contain whitespace or a leading plus sign.
items.rationale: A narrow token grammar keeps promised behavior explicit.
acceptance: 0, 007, and -12 satisfy the token grammar.
A token with a leading plus sign is outside the token grammar.
A token containing whitespace is outside the token grammar.

source_notes.text: The implementation decisions define ASCII digits, optional leading minus, and excluded whitespace and plus signs.
The Integer Token glossary entry gives the same bounded lexical definition.

items.title: Supported delimiter set
items.statement: A Delimiter MUST be exactly one comma character or one actual line-feed character between adjacent Integer Tokens.
items.rationale: The first release supports exactly two delimiter forms.
acceptance: A comma between tokens is a supported delimiter.
An actual line-feed between tokens is a supported delimiter.
Custom delimiter declarations are not part of the supported delimiter set.

source_notes.text: The source limits delimiters to a comma or actual line-feed.
The Delimiter glossary entry defines the same two characters and excludes custom delimiters.

items.title: One calculation path
items.statement: The command-line adapter MUST delegate to the public add operation and MUST NOT implement an independent parser or calculation path.
items.rationale: Shared behavior prevents Python and command-line semantics from drifting.
acceptance: Inspection shows the CLI invokes the public add operation.
There is no second CLI-specific Number List parser.
Python and CLI supported behavior is produced by the same calculation implementation.

source_notes.text: User story 19 and the implementation decisions require the CLI to delegate to public add.

items.title: Tests use public seams
items.statement: Release tests MUST exercise externally visible behavior through the public add operation and installed command rather than depending on parser structure or helper calls.
items.rationale: Implementation details should remain changeable without invalidating the contract suite.
acceptance: The primary suite imports and calls public add.
The secondary suite invokes the installed command through subprocesses.
Tests do not require a named private parser, helper call, or module organization.

source_notes.text: User story 20 and Testing Decisions require tests of externally visible behavior, not implementation organization.

items.title: Explicit supported partitions
items.statement: The public Python test suite MUST explicitly cover every promised supported behavior partition and negative rejection ordering and duplication.
items.rationale: Acceptance cannot depend on only a few representative examples.
acceptance: Coverage includes empty, single, many, comma, line-feed, mixed, zero, leading-zero, and negative-zero inputs.
Coverage includes complete negative occurrence order and duplicate preservation.
Malformed Input behavior is not asserted as a stable product result.

source_notes.text: User story 21 and Testing Decisions enumerate the public behavior partitions that require explicit coverage.

items.title: Focused installed-command verification
items.statement: A small subprocess suite MUST verify installed-command success output and status, actual line-feed handling, and negative rejection channels without duplicating every Python case.
items.rationale: The secondary seam needs direct evidence while the primary seam retains exhaustive behavior coverage.
acceptance: At least one successful command case checks stdout, stderr, and status.
At least one command case supplies an actual line-feed delimiter.
At least one negative command case checks stderr, empty stdout, and nonzero status.

source_notes.text: Testing Decisions prescribe a small command subprocess suite with these three areas of evidence.

items.title: Same local and hosted gate
items.statement: Local verification and GitHub Actions MUST run the same uv-only release gate: uv lock --check, frozen Ruff checks, frozen ty checks, and frozen pytest.
items.rationale: Local and hosted evidence must be comparable.
acceptance: A documented local gate runs uv lock --check.
The gate runs uv run --frozen ruff check ., uv run --frozen ty check, and uv run --frozen pytest.
GitHub Actions invokes the same quality checks rather than a weaker subset.

source_notes.text: User story 22 and Testing Decisions prescribe identical local and GitHub Actions quality gates.

items.title: Verified commit identity
items.statement: Completion evidence MUST identify the exact commit whose release gate succeeded.
items.rationale: Reviewers need an unambiguous binding between evidence and source state.
acceptance: Completion evidence records a full commit identifier.
The recorded identifier names the source state on which the reported gate ran.
A reviewer can distinguish the verified commit from later repository changes.

source_notes.text: User story 23 and Testing Decisions require exact verified commit identification in completion evidence.

items.title: Visible incremental TDD progression
items.statement: Delivery evidence MUST show captured failing and passing public-contract tests that make incremental red-green progression auditable without requiring a particular commit cadence.
items.rationale: Human reviewers need evidence of the claimed TDD journey at durable product seams.
acceptance: Evidence contains at least one failing public-contract test observation before its corresponding behavior passes.
Evidence contains the later passing result at the same public seam.
Review does not infer TDD solely from the final green suite or require one commit per cycle.

source_notes.text: User story 24 and Testing Decisions require captured red-green public-contract evidence but no particular commit cadence.

items.title: Human-owned acceptance
items.statement: Human review MUST own acceptance of the Specification, Authority, planning artifacts, and delivered release.
items.rationale: Automated structuring and verification provide evidence but do not replace human acceptance decisions.
acceptance: The Specification is presented for human review before it becomes accepted authority input.
Planning and release evidence remain available for human review.
No automated test result is represented as the human acceptance decision itself.

source_notes.text: Further Notes assign acceptance of Specification, Authority, planning artifacts, and release to human review.

items.title: Python 3.13 or newer
items.statement: The project MUST target Python 3.13 or newer.
items.rationale: The source establishes the supported runtime baseline.
acceptance: Project metadata declares a minimum Python version of 3.13 or newer.
The release gate executes under a supported Python version.
No promised compatibility with older Python versions is introduced.

source_notes.text: Implementation Decisions explicitly target Python 3.13 or newer.

items.title: Exclusive uv project workflow
items.statement: Project dependency management, locking, command execution, and release verification MUST use uv exclusively.
items.rationale: One toolchain keeps local and hosted workflows repeatable.
acceptance: The project contains uv-compatible metadata and a lock file.
Documented quality commands execute through uv with frozen dependencies where specified.
No second package-manager workflow is required for the release.

source_notes.text: Implementation Decisions require exclusive uv management and Testing Decisions define the uv-only gate.

items.title: Standard library preference
items.statement: The implementation SHOULD use the Python standard library and MAY add a runtime dependency only for a concrete requirement that cannot reasonably be met without it.
items.rationale: The bounded calculator does not justify unnecessary runtime dependencies.
acceptance: Runtime dependencies are absent unless each is tied to a concrete requirement.
Any runtime dependency has a recorded reason the standard library is not reasonable.
Development tooling is not misrepresented as a product runtime requirement.

source_notes.text: Implementation Decisions prefer the Python standard library and permit a dependency only for a concrete unmet requirement.

items.title: No typing suppressions
items.statement: The uv-only quality gate MUST pass without typing suppressions.
items.rationale: Type evidence must not be created by silencing reported problems.
acceptance: The ty check succeeds in the release gate.
Calculator source contains no suppression added to bypass a reported typing failure.
Hosted verification applies the same typing standard as local verification.

source_notes.text: Implementation Decisions require the uv-only quality gate without typing suppressions.

items.title: ValueError is the Python rejection seam
items.statement: Use ValueError from the public add operation to represent a Negative-number Rejection.
items.rationale: The source explicitly selects this built-in error rather than a partial result or custom return shape.

source_notes.text: Implementation Decisions specify that public add raises ValueError for parsed values below zero.

items.title: Public add is the primary test seam
items.statement: Use the public Python add operation as the primary behavioral test seam and the installed command as a focused secondary seam.
items.rationale: This arrangement covers product behavior deeply while directly checking adapter integration.

source_notes.text: Testing Decisions select public add as primary and the installed command through a small subprocess suite as secondary.

items.title: Custom delimiters excluded
items.statement: Custom delimiter declarations and custom delimiter behavior are outside the first release.
items.rationale: They belong to a later kata stage and are not implicit requirements.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope explicitly excludes custom delimiters.
The Delimiter glossary entry says custom delimiters are outside the active Product Goal.

items.title: No special meaning above 1000
items.statement: Values above 1000 receive no special ignoring or transformation behavior and remain ordinary Integer Tokens in this release.
items.rationale: The later kata rule for large values is explicitly excluded.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope states that values above 1000 remain ordinary Integer Tokens rather than being ignored.

items.title: No expression evaluation
items.statement: Arithmetic expressions and general expression evaluation are outside the first release.
items.rationale: The product is a String Calculator over Number Lists, not a formula engine.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope excludes arithmetic expressions and general expression evaluation.
The String Calculator and Number List glossary entries warn against expression-evaluator language.

items.title: No additional calculator operations
items.statement: Subtraction, multiplication, division, and other calculator operations are outside the first release.
items.rationale: The reviewed solution exposes one summing operation only.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope excludes additional calculator operations.

items.title: No web or graphical interface
items.statement: A web interface and graphical user interface are outside the first release.
items.rationale: The agreed product interfaces are Python and the installed command only.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope explicitly excludes web and graphical interfaces.

items.title: No persistence, accounts, networking, or services
items.statement: Persistence, user accounts, networking, and service infrastructure are outside the first release.
items.rationale: The calculator is a local bounded operation and command.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope excludes persistence, accounts, networking, and services.

items.title: Malformed Input behavior is unspecified
items.statement: The release does not establish stable behavior or diagnostics for Malformed Input, including whitespace, leading plus signs, adjacent or trailing delimiters, or unsupported command argument counts.
items.rationale: These cases are deliberately outside the promised product contract.

source_notes.text: Implementation and Testing Decisions leave Malformed Input outside the stable contract and enumerate representative unsupported forms.
Malformed Input is defined as outside the current Product Goal.

items.title: Literal backslash-n behavior is unspecified
items.statement: Stable handling of the two-character sequence consisting of backslash followed by n is outside the first release.
items.rationale: Only an actual line-feed character is a supported Delimiter.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope excludes stable behavior for the two-character backslash-n sequence.

items.title: Planning decisions remain downstream
items.statement: Sprint duration, story-point capacity, task decomposition, and implementation sequencing are outside this Specification and remain owned by AgileForge planning after Specification and Authority acceptance.
items.rationale: The Specification defines product and verification behavior, not downstream planning commitments.

source_notes.text: Out of Scope explicitly leaves sprint duration, story-point capacity, task decomposition, and sequencing to later AgileForge planning.

items.title: Empty and single-token examples
items.statement: Examples: add an empty string to obtain 0; add 7 to obtain 7; add 0007 to obtain 7.
items.rationale: These examples distinguish empty, ordinary single-token, and leading-zero semantics.

source_notes.text: The examples instantiate user stories for empty input, one token, and leading zeros without adding new behavior.

items.title: Supported delimiter examples
items.statement: Examples: add 1,2,3 to obtain 6; add three tokens split by actual line feeds to obtain their sum; combine a line feed and comma in one list to obtain one total.
items.rationale: These examples demonstrate each supported delimiter partition.

source_notes.text: The examples instantiate comma, line-feed, and mixed-delimiter user stories.

items.title: Complete canonical rejection example
items.statement: Example: adding -01,2,-003,-01 raises ValueError with negative numbers not allowed: -1, -3, -1.
items.rationale: One example demonstrates full rejection, canonical rendering, encounter order, and duplicate preservation.

source_notes.text: The example combines only the source-defined rejection rules for all occurrences, canonical values, order, and duplicates.

items.title: Successful command example
items.statement: Example: invoking string-calculator with positional argument 1,2 writes exactly 3 and one newline to standard output, writes nothing to standard error, and exits zero.
items.rationale: This is the minimal observable command success contract.

source_notes.text: The example directly instantiates the documented CLI success behavior.

items.title: Rejected command example
items.statement: Example: invoking string-calculator with positional argument -1,2 writes negative numbers not allowed: -1 and one newline to standard error, writes nothing to standard output, and exits nonzero.
items.rationale: This is the minimal observable command rejection contract.

source_notes.text: The example directly instantiates the documented CLI negative-input behavior.

Provides multiline list summation.

Provides the scriptable command entry point.

Creates comparable local and hosted evidence.

All release-gate commands use the selected project tool.

controlled_terms.definition: A calculator that accepts one Number List and returns its arithmetic sum or a Negative-number Rejection.
Text containing zero or more Integer Tokens separated by Delimiters; an empty Number List represents zero.
A decimal integer written with ASCII digits and an optional leading minus sign, without whitespace or a leading plus sign.
A comma or actual line-feed character separating adjacent Integer Tokens in a Number List.
The non-success result for a Number List containing values below zero, reporting every canonical negative occurrence in encounter order including duplicates.
Text that is neither empty nor a valid Number List and whose handling is outside the current release contract.
